etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Latin complicatus, past participle of complicare (“to fold together”), from com- (“together”) + plicare (“to fold, weave, knit”); see plaid, and compare complex.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To make complex; to modify so as to make something intricate or difficult.

quote.citation: 1896, Arthur Edward Waite, “Chapter 14”, in Devil-Worship in France, or the Question of Lucifer:
quote.text: Let us, however, put aside for the moment the mendacities and forgeries which complicate the question of Lucifer, and let us approach Palladism from an altogether different side.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To involve in a convoluted matter.

quote.text: How poor, how rich, how abject, how august, / How complicate, how wonderful, is Man!
